investigator.value: Lisa Guillory, a recovering addict and widow navigating her internal psychological unraveling
investigator.quote: Lisa Guillory's dreams are indistinct and do not contain the images normally associated with nightmares.

red_herring.value: Herman fabricates a debt and theft accusation against Lisa — claiming she stole $2,300 from Rodney's cashbox and owes $8,000 — to coerce her into prostitution/drug running, a false trail that misdirects Lisa (and reader) about whether she actually committed these acts.
red_herring.quote: 'Cause you was so stoned out you got no memory of it... I'll do anyt'ing, Herman. I'll pay you tomorrow, Herman.'

social_world.value: Post-Katrina south Louisiana underclass: a hierarchy running from pimp-exploiter Herman Stanga (controlling crack queens, debt bondage, caterer cousin Rodney) down through addicts and war widows; AA sponsor networks as counter-institution; National Guard losses flattening individual grief into communal numbness; government indifference to insurance payouts.
social_world.quote: Herman prefers them white because there are black dudes who will always pay top dollar for white bread, no matter what kind of package.

alibi.value: Lisa tells Tookie she is not going to use and is late for the employment office — a partial truth used to evade accountability; later Herman constructs a false alibi-in-reverse for Lisa, asserting she was present and lucid enough to steal from Rodney's cashbox, which she denies.
alibi.quote: 'I'm late for my appointment at the employment office.' / 'I ain't stole no money out of no office.'

reveal_mechanic.value: The knocking sound — Lisa's recurring auditory hallucination — is retroactively revealed as the literal memory of her sister and unbaptized child trapped and drowning beneath the Katrina floodwaters, disclosed only in the final dream-vision; the reader re-interprets all prior mentions of the sound through this single climactic confession.
reveal_mechanic.quote: My sister was trying to hand up my li'l boy t'rou the hole in the roof, and they fell back in the water. I could hear them knocking.

media_and_audience.value: The AA meeting congregation functions as a de facto audience that has heard so many Iraq-casualty stories that Lisa's grief is received with antagonism or boredom rather than sympathy; communal over-saturation of trauma narratives neutralises individual testimony and denies Lisa the public acknowledgement she seeks.
media_and_audience.quote: The local National Guard unit lost five members in Iraq in one day alone, and no one has a patent now on stories of wounded and maimed and dead GIs.

investigator_wound.value: Lisa is simultaneously the protagonist-investigator of her own survival and the wound itself: she cannot process Gerald's death, her drowned child, or Katrina because she is the last witness to all three; her addiction is the direct symptom of unprocessed guilt over her unbaptised child's death, which she can only approach obliquely through the knocking sound.
investigator_wound.quote: My baby never got baptized. These t'ings ain't your fault, Lisa... You ain't learned that, you?
